Not interested in what exactly? (Pause)
If they say "whatever this is": Got it. I think we're on two different pages. What's your actual understanding of mortgage protection?
If they're wrong: That's exactly why I'm assigned to you — to give you the full picture, because that's not exactly what this is.
If they're close: You're close. But there are a few parts most homeowners don't know about, especially the living benefits and payment protection side.
Transition: This is why I only need about 10 to 15 minutes to show you what applies to your situation. Once you see it, it'll make more sense.
followup: What have you heard about mortgage protection so far?

response:
I do have to go over it with you. You don't automatically qualify for anything, but this is the time I'm assigned to review the options with you. Let me ask you — is this your first home?

If yes: That makes sense. They throw a lot at you during the mortgage process. The bank makes sure they're protected, but this is the part that protects your household.

If no: Got it. Then you probably remember the bank protects itself first. Since COVID, these mortgage protection options became much more common, especially when someone gets a new loan, refinance, or HELOC.
followup: Was this mortgage from a purchase, a refinance, or a home-equity line?

title: What is this about?
triggers: can you explain why you're calling
response: This is your state-regulated mortgage protection/payment protection review. These benefits can include paying off the mortgage in case of death, helping make mortgage payments if you're disabled and can't work, and in some programs, returning premiums if the coverage is never used. You can look into it later, but it may be subject to more underwriting, higher rates, or medical exams. That's why I'm assigned to go over it with you now. Let me ask you — is this a new purchase, a refinance, or a line of credit?
followup: Was your home recently purchased, refinanced, or did you open a home-equity line?

title: Do I have to pay for this?

response: You do have to qualify first. It's not automatic. But unlike homeowners insurance or PMI, these programs are designed to be affordable and unnoticeable inside the monthly budget. I'll know in the next few minutes what they have available for you. If it makes sense, great. If not, at least you'll know what your options are.
followup: Would it help if we first looked at the coverage amount you would want to protect?

title: I can't afford it
triggers: i don't have room in my budget

response: I understand. Things are expensive today. But let me ask you this — if things are tight now, what would they look like if something happened tomorrow and your income stopped? This is designed for regular working families. If you had hundreds of thousands sitting in the bank, this probably wouldn't be as important. But for most people, losing one income or missing payments would make things very difficult very quickly. That's why we look at something affordable that protects the mortgage and gives your household breathing room.
followup: Would you be comfortable reviewing an option only if the premium fit your budget?

response: A lot of people say that, and selling may still be the plan. The issue is, your family can't just snap their fingers and sell the home overnight. And if they're forced to sell quickly, they may lose tens of thousands in equity just to get it off their hands. Even a smaller amount of protection can buy them time — time to make the right decision instead of being forced into the wrong one. So this isn't always about keeping the house forever. Sometimes it's about giving your family options.
followup: Would your priority be helping them keep the home, or giving them financial flexibility?

To be honest, your bank doesn't really care whether you have mortgage protection because it doesn't benefit them. It benefits you. Homeowners insurance and PMI protect the bank. This protects your family from the bank if something happens and the payments can't be made. I'm the person assigned to walk you through what's available, kind of like when you did homeowners insurance through a third party. I don't have a bias either way. I just have to show you what you qualify for. Let me ask you — what's your current understanding of mortgage protection?

title: I already have homeowners insurance or PMI
triggers: my homeowners policy covers the house
my lender has insurance on the property
i have insurance with my mortgage
my homeowners insurance should cover that
response: Perfect, and that's important. Homeowners insurance protects the property from things like fire, storms, and damage. PMI protects the lender if you didn't put enough down. Neither one pays your family, makes the mortgage payment for you, or pays off the home if something happens to you. That's the gap this review is designed to address.
followup: Do you mean homeowners insurance, PMI, or an individual life insurance policy?

Stronger version: Let me ask you this — is your mortgage broker going to make the payments if you get hurt, sick, or pass away? Probably not. And that's exactly why I'm assigned to go over this with you. This isn't about whether they were right or wrong. It's just that this part protects your household, not the bank, not the realtor, and not the lender.
followup: Did they discuss any personal life coverage with you, or mainly the loan and closing?

response: The face amount is the policy's stated death benefit, subject to the contract's terms, and the benefit is generally paid to the named beneficiary or beneficiaries if the insured dies while coverage is in force. Loans, outstanding interest, exclusions, and other policy provisions may affect the amount paid. The exact details depend on the policy.
followup: Would you like to focus on who receives the benefit or how much coverage might be appropriate?
